restrictions.rule: Exported signatures and context-sensitive empty collections must carry enough source type information for deterministic target spelling.
Runtime globals and members must have a binding in flight-runtime-contract/2; dynamic prototype extension, eval, and ambient reflection are outside the profile.
Computed object access and open-ended JavaScript property-key coercion require lowering before C++ emission.

Closed multi-member unions require distinct C++ alternative representations. Typeof and discriminant access requires checker proof; type assertions use checked access. Alternatives that collapse to the same C++ type, and unions combining several values with null or undefined, remain excluded.
Captured binding reassignment uses shared cells. Referent mutation is supported only for flight-cpp containers with shared reference identity; value-represented structural objects remain excluded.
A captured mutable binding must have initialized, concretely typed storage; uninitialized and captured for-in bindings remain excluded until absence and iteration storage are explicit.
Relative imports must be compiled as one resolved module graph and provided to the downstream include path.
Non-ASCII case conversion requires a host Unicode service with pinned data and application-level conformance tests.
Date support is limited to epoch instants and UTC calendar projection until a local civil-time policy is elected.
